ranking_basis: Qualitative usefulness for the next structural test, not probability of a kinship meaning

candidates.candidate: qi-tu-ne / ma-ka-ri-te headers with di-ki-se as an entry
observations: HT117a .1–2 includes ma-ka-ri-te; HT117b .1 has qi-tu-ne, and .2 has di-ki-se 1.
HT87 .1–2 combines qi-tu-ne and ma-ka-ri-te in its header; .3 has di-ki-se 1. GORILA I pp.197, 199, 137.
candidates.best_supported_structure: Repeated header-to-entry association; a candidate administrative classification

rivals.occupation: A work category could select the same individual or designation on both lists.
rivals.ownership_or_responsibility: A responsible person or household label could govern the listed entries.
rivals.place: A location or affiliation could group the same entries.
rivals.kinship: Family affiliation is logically possible, but the header is not independently identified as a relative or a personal name. No second named participant or relational alternation is established.

candidates.decision: Best structural follow-up; retain UNKNOWN relation. Shared header/entry membership alone cannot choose among rivals.

candidates.candidate: da-si-*118 and qa-A310-i change counts across lists
observations: da-si-*118 has 24 on HT85a .3–4 and 2 on HT122a .2.
qa-A310-i has 1 on HT85b .5–6 and 3 on HT122a .4. GORILA I pp.131, 133, 207.
candidates.best_supported_structure: Labels associated with variable counted quantities; a numeral 1 does not certify a unique individual

rivals.occupation: A group designation permits several counted workers.
rivals.ownership_or_responsibility: An individual supervisor or owner can also head a count of several dependants or goods.
rivals.place: A locality can contribute several counted units.
rivals.kinship: A household designation could also head several people, but no parent-child relation is identified.

candidates.decision: Useful negative against name-by-quantity heuristics; cannot decide occupation versus place versus responsible person. No new sound equivalence is needed for these exact strings.

candidates.candidate: HT85b pa, ka and di logograms near qe-ka and te-tu
observations: AB77 + 1 and AB07 + 1 follow damaged te-tu + 1 on physical .2–3; GORILA I p.133.
candidates.best_supported_structure: Possible subordinate designations, with three separate quantities

rivals.occupation: Abbreviated work or personnel categories are compatible with single-sign logograms.
rivals.ownership_or_responsibility: The preceding entry may organize subordinate categories or responsibilities.
rivals.place: An abbreviated affiliation cannot be excluded.
rivals.kinship: An unnamed relative could in principle be represented by a designation, but no controlled replacement of a second name is observed. Pa, ka and di are conventional sign readings, not kinship words.

candidates.decision: Keep as low-support layout evidence, one object only. Do not force a two-name CHILD_OF representation or infer daughter from a single sign.

candidates.candidate: HT117 individual-entry hypothesis and proposed Linear B name parallels
observations: HT117 has 17 lexical entries counted as 1 across three sections, on one physical object.
ku-*56-nu also appears beneath ki-ro on HT88 (physical .5), matching its HT117a header context; GORILA I pp.139, 197.
candidates.best_supported_structure: Possible individual slots; contextual recurrence, not a personal-name gold standard

rivals.occupation: An occupational designation can stand in an individual entry.
rivals.ownership_or_responsibility: A named recipient or owner could produce the same list shape.
rivals.place: An affiliation label may be counted without being a person's name.
rivals.kinship: A relative-designation could replace a name, but no contrast here identifies that meaning or the relative's gender.

candidates.decision: Keep possible person/designation slots without gold personal-name or gender labels. Proposed phonetic parallels are not independent validation after the previous correspondence gate failed.

scope_limit: No convincing named or unnamed-parentage formula in this small audited set; not evidence that Linear A lacks kinship formulas.
